sources.title: Earth Sphere Federation
sources.author: Gundam 00 Wiki contributors
sources.access_method: Bounded public plot, character or episode passage read
sources.read_scope: Energy infrastructure and improved member-state living standards coexist with dictatorship and excluded poverty.
sources.limitations: Power generation and Veda’s information control are not a complete material-access constitution.

sources.title: Photon Battery
sources.author: Gundam Wiki contributors
sources.access_method: Bounded public plot, character or episode passage read
sources.read_scope: Venus Globe manufactures batteries and Capital Tower regulates their distribution; some supplies are freely distributed to Towasanga.
sources.limitations: An energy flow is not necessarily a free universal floor of food, shelter and care. A Venus Globe direct open returned 402 and was respected.

sources.title: Casshan
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.access_method: Bounded public plot, character or episode passage read
sources.read_scope: Service automatons rebel, while a human-derived android fights them.
sources.limitations: The original series differs from the 1993 OVA, Casshern Sins and the 2004 film; robotic bodies do not erase human-derived activity.

sources.title: Casshern Sins
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.access_method: Bounded public plot, character or episode passage read
sources.read_scope: Ruin affects robots and Luna selectively heals people/robots.
sources.limitations: Immortality or a selected cure is not a general autonomous material-production constitution; unlike the original, this has its own world.

sources.title: Casshern 2004
sources.author: Melbourne International Film Festival archive
sources.access_method: Bounded public plot, character or episode passage read
sources.read_scope: An industrial military state and regenerative research produce neo-sapiens amid war.
sources.limitations: The film’s military and biological mutation premise does not establish a civilian post-work economy.

sources.title: Neo Tokyo: Construction Cancellation Order
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors via indexed mirror
sources.access_method: Bounded public plot, character or episode passage read
sources.read_scope: An autonomous construction site continues its contract while a salaryman tries to stop it.
sources.limitations: Only this segment is used. An unstoppable job site is not a durable supported resident society.

sources.title: Yokohama Kaidashi Kikou
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.access_method: Bounded public plot, character or episode passage read
sources.read_scope: Alpha is a robot person running a café amid declining human society.
sources.limitations: One working artificial person and a peaceful setting do not establish general post-work material access.

sources.title: Aria
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.access_method: Bounded public plot, character or episode passage read
sources.read_scope: Terraforming permits Aqua settlement; gondoliers and other people perform useful tourist work.

decisions.reason: Eden’s computer-supervised city does not establish ordinary access independent of useful human work.
decisions.analysis: Construction and network governance alone do not supply wages, entitlements or control over material production.
decisions.follow_up: Record the short gap/comparison and continue; do not reconstruct an entire franchise to rescue the lead.

decisions.reason: Moonrace hibernation does not establish a post-work active population.
decisions.analysis: The short reference does not settle awake residents’ food/housing provision or participation.
decisions.follow_up: Record the short gap/comparison and continue; do not reconstruct an entire franchise to rescue the lead.

decisions.reason: Veda-directed politics and abundant energy do not establish a labor-independent civilian support floor.
decisions.analysis: Different ESF membership and political periods have different conditions; dictatorship is not an economic allocation mechanism.
decisions.follow_up: Record the short gap/comparison and continue; do not reconstruct an entire franchise to rescue the lead.

decisions.reason: Venus Globe’s advanced battery industry does not establish household access or a justified participation estimate.
decisions.analysis: An energy-producing civilization still needs its actual labor/property rules verified.
decisions.follow_up: Record the short gap/comparison and continue; do not reconstruct an entire franchise to rescue the lead.

decisions.reason: Capital Tower’s controlled energy distribution does not establish complete ordinary material provision.
decisions.analysis: Even free energy to one recipient does not imply free food, housing and care for all people.
decisions.follow_up: Record the short gap/comparison and continue; do not reconstruct an entire franchise to rescue the lead.

decisions.reason: Robot rebellion and human submission do not establish a supported living human post-work order.
decisions.analysis: The original series’ conflict is not the separate restoration society in Sins.
decisions.follow_up: Record the short gap/comparison and continue; do not reconstruct an entire franchise to rescue the lead.

decisions.reason: Decaying artificial persons do not automatically constitute a post-work human economy.
decisions.analysis: Ruin and survival are real, but an applicable supported-person population and its production/access system are missing.
decisions.follow_up: Record the short gap/comparison and continue; do not reconstruct an entire franchise to rescue the lead.

decisions.reason: Luna’s selective healing does not establish the restoration society’s wider material economy.
decisions.analysis: Treating bodies or granting longevity is not automatically technological replacement of production work or a universal support order.
decisions.follow_up: Record the short gap/comparison and continue; do not reconstruct an entire franchise to rescue the lead.

decisions.reason: Industrial war, regeneration and neo-sapiens do not establish a post-work civilian distribution system.
decisions.analysis: Biological resurrection and military technology are not sufficient for admission.
decisions.follow_up: Record the short gap/comparison and continue; do not reconstruct an entire franchise to rescue the lead.

decisions.reason: The construction project is a workplace without an established supported resident population.
decisions.analysis: A temporarily endangered salaryman is not a durable post-work society, even though construction is fully automatic.
decisions.follow_up: Record the short gap/comparison and continue; do not reconstruct an entire franchise to rescue the lead.

decisions.reason: Robot assistance and a peaceful decline do not establish general work-independent necessities.
decisions.analysis: A café operated by a robot person remains useful work and cannot stand for an entire population’s resource access.
decisions.follow_up: Record the short gap/comparison and continue; do not reconstruct an entire franchise to rescue the lead.

decisions.reason: Aqua’s terraforming and tourism do not verify the discovery claim of a robot-supported human economy.
decisions.analysis: Human-guided gondolas provide valued real service; old-fashioned technology is not automatically employment-preserving make-work.
decisions.follow_up: Record the short gap/comparison and continue; do not reconstruct an entire franchise to rescue the lead.

review_notes: Twelve fast dispositions and ten scoped source records; no whole fiction or episode transcript read.
Hibernation, energy abundance, body restoration and automatic construction are not interchangeable with a living population’s labor-independent material access.

An Aria/Yokohama crossover fanfiction explicitly invented the desired robot economy; it was discarded rather than mistaken for canon. Gundam crossover/fanon and unrelated series references were likewise excluded.
The original Casshan reference was checked separately to avoid importing a 1993 OVA or Sins premise.
